title: Affine and stalk integral-closure models of finite normalization
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a reduced finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $
u:X^
u	o X$ be its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. Then $X$ and $X^
u$ are Noetherian (their affine section rings satisfy the ascending chain condition on ideals and their underlying spaces are quasi-compact), $X$ has finitely many irreducible components, and $
u$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The locus $N$ of points whose local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] is dense open, $
u^{-1}N	o N$ is an isomorphism, and normalization restricts to every open subscheme. For every nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], list its minimal prime ideals as $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_t$, put $K_i=\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p_i)$ and let $B_i$ be the integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] of $R/\mathfrak p_i$ in $K_i$. If $T=\Gamma(
u^{-1}U,\mathcal O_{X^
u})$, there are canonical identifications
$$T=\prod_{i=1}^t B_i\subseteq Q(R)=\prod_{i=1}^t K_i,$$
under which $R	o T$ is the injective structural map and $T$ is its integral closure in $Q(R)$ and is finite as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Here $Q(D)$ denotes the localization of a reduced ring $D$ at all its non-zero-divisors. For $x\in U$ corresponding to a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, set $A_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $C_x=(
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u})_x$. Canonically,
$$A_x=R_{\mathfrak p},\quad C_x=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}T\subseteq Q(A_x)=\prod_{\mathfrak p_i\subseteq\mathfrak p}K_i.$$
The ring $A_x$ is reduced Noetherian and $C_x$ is the finite integral closure of $A_x$ in $Q(A_x)$, with its structural inclusion. These identifications respect the maps induced by restriction and localization. If $X$ is empty all pointwise assertions are vacuous and $
u$ is the empty morphism.

source.place: Tag 0C3B (lemma-stalk-normalization), Tag 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components); varieties.tex Tag 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic), specialized to reduced finite-type schemes over a field.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: $X$ is Noetherian. Its irreducible components are finite in number by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components], and every affine open ring is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. Reducedness of these rings follows from [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Each reduced component $Z_j$ is integral by [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] and is of finite type over $k$: a finite affine cover of $X$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras restricts to the finite affine cover of $Z_j$ by their quotient algebras. Thus [lem-sc-normalization-exists] applies to each $Z_j$, giving a finite, surjective normalization $Z_j^\nu\to Z_j$.

Normalization restricts to every open $V\subseteq X$. Indeed the components of $V$ are exactly the nonempty $Z_j\cap V$: [lem-sc-components-open-injection] gives that these intersections are distinct components, and [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] gives exhaustiveness. A nonempty open of the integral scheme $Z_j$ has the same function field, as identified on its affine opens by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. In the construction [def-sc-normalization], restricting the integral-closure sheaf to this open restricts the base ring and keeps this field; hence its relative spectrum is precisely $(Z_j^
u)|_{Z_j\cap V}$. Taking the disjoint union in [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] gives $X^
u	imes_XV=V^
u$, with its structural map. These are identifications of the constructed maps, not merely abstract isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components); Tag 035E (definition-normalization); restriction of the integral-closure sheaf

proof.text:
Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be affine. By Step 1, $R$ is reduced Noetherian, so [lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal] with the ideal $0$ gives finitely many minimal primes $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_t$, and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] shows that the components of $U$ are the $V(\mathfrak p_i)$, without repetition. By Step 2 these are the $Z_i\cap U$ for the distinct components $Z_i$ of $X$ meeting $U$. As $\mathfrak p_i$ is the radical ideal with $V(\mathfrak p_i)=Z_i\cap U$, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] (1), (2) identifies the open $Z_i\cap U$ of the reduced induced $Z_i$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathfrak p_i)$, over $U$ via $R	o R/\mathfrak p_i$. By [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], $
u^{-1}U$ is the disjoint union of the opens $W_i\subseteq Z_i^
u$ lying over $Z_i\cap U$; summands of components missing $U$ contribute nothing. Step 1 makes $Z_i^
u	o Z_i$ finite, so [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] gives $W_i=\operatorname{Spec}T_i$ with $T_i$ a finite $R/\mathfrak p_i$-module, hence a finite $R$-module: lift the coefficients of a generating family through the quotient. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] and [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $
u^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}T$ with $T=\prod_iT_i$ and structural map $r\mapsto(r mod\mathfrak p_i)_i$; the coordinate embeddings of the generating families generate $T$ over $R$. Hence $
u$ is finite, by that same definition. If $U=\varnothing$, then $t=0$ and $T=0$.

$
u$ is surjective by [lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-generic-properties], as $X$ is locally Noetherian. Module generators of $T$ also generate it as an $R$-algebra, so $T$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; the finite affine cover of Step 1 has affine inverse images, so $X^
u$ is Noetherian. Every quasi-compact open of $X$ is Noetherian, hence has finitely many components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. Thus [lem-sfb-normalization-affine-total-fractions] applies: $
u^{-1}U\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\overline R$ over $U$, with $\overline R$ the integral closure of $R$ in $Q(R)$, and [def-weil-affine-spectrum] turns this into an $R$-algebra isomorphism $T\simeq\overline R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions], $Q(R)=\prod_iR_{\mathfrak p_i}=\prod_iK_i$: the reduced local ring at a minimal prime is a field, and its map from $R/\mathfrak p_i$ inverts exactly the nonzero elements. $R	o Q(R)$ is injective: $r/1=0$ means $sr=0$ for a non-zero-divisor $s$, so $r=0$. A tuple $(x_i)\in\prod_iK_i$ is integral over $R$ iff each $x_i$ is integral over $R/\mathfrak p_i$: project a monic equation; conversely lift monic equations of the $x_i$ to monic $F_i$ over $R$, and $\prod_iF_i$ kills $(x_i)$ coordinatewise. So $\overline R=\prod_iB_i$. Any $R$-algebra map $\varphi:\overline R	o Q(R)$ is the inclusion: for $b=r/s$, $s\varphi(b)=r$ with $s$ a unit. Hence $T=\prod_iB_i\subseteq Q(R)$, $R	o T$ is injective, and $T$ is the integral closure, finite by Step 3. The idempotent of $T_i$ is killed by an element of $\mathfrak p_i$ outside the other (incomparable) minimal primes, so $T_i$ is the factor $B_i$.

Fix $x\in U$ with prime $\mathfrak p$ and put $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-sc-affine-pushforward-stalk-localization], the germ maps identify $A_x=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $C_x=S^{-1}T$, with their given structural map. The first ring is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-preserves-reduced]. If $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ generate $T$ over $R$, their images $b_j/1$ generate $S^{-1}T$ over $S^{-1}R$: localize an expression $b=\sum r_jb_j$ and divide its coefficients by $s$. In particular $C_x$ is finite over $A_x$.

source.place: Tag 0C3B (lemma-stalk-normalization); perfect.tex Tag 0AVW (lemma-affine-morphism-equivalence), affine stalk paragraph

proof.text: Localizing $Q(R)=\prod_iK_i$ at $S$ deletes precisely the factors with $\mathfrak p_i\not\subseteq\mathfrak p$. For such an $i$, choose $s_i\in\mathfrak p_i\setminus\mathfrak p$; it becomes zero in $K_i$ and is inverted, killing that factor. For a surviving factor every $s\in S$ is already a nonzero unit. Localization commutes with this finite product directly: a tuple of fractions has the common denominator given by the product of its finitely many denominators, and the same operation witnesses equality of tuples. By [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization], the minimal primes of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ are exactly $\mathfrak p_iR_{\mathfrak p}$ with $\mathfrak p_i\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Their minimal-prime localizations are $R_{\mathfrak p_i}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localize-localization-at-prime]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions] to $A_x$ therefore identifies $Q(A_x)=\prod_{\mathfrak p_i\subseteq\mathfrak p}K_i=S^{-1}Q(R)$, canonically over $R$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], applied to $R\to Q(R)$, identifies $S^{-1}T$ injectively with the integral closure of $S^{-1}R$ in this ring. Together with Step 5 this gives exactly the required $C_x\subseteq Q(A_x)$ and its finite integral-closure property.

On $U$ put $M=T/R$, a finite $R$-module since the images of generators of $T$ generate its quotient. Localized fractions give $M_{\mathfrak p}=C_x/A_x$: the map $b/s\mapsto(b+R)/s$ is surjective, and its kernel consists of fractions for which some multiple of the numerator lies in $R$, exactly the image of $R_{\mathfrak p}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-normal-iff-integrally-closed-total-fractions] and Step 6, $M_{\mathfrak p}=0$ is equivalent to $A_x$ being normal; for this local ring, normality is equivalent to being an integrally closed domain, using [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. Thus $N\cap U$ is the complement of $\operatorname{Supp}M$, which is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator]. This proves openness of $N$. At each minimal prime $\mathfrak p_i$, the local ring is the field $K_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field], so every generic point belongs to $N$. Their closures cover $X$, hence $N$ is dense. For $x\in N\cap U$, the support formula supplies $a\in\operatorname{Ann}_R(M)\setminus\mathfrak p$. Then $M_a=0$, so $T_a=R_a$ and $\nu^{-1}D(a)\to D(a)$ is an isomorphism. These neighborhoods cover $N$; the isomorphisms are induced by the structural map, and their inverses agree on overlaps. Consequently $\nu^{-1}N\to N$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: algebra.tex Tags 030C (lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal), 00L2 (lemma-support-closed), 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring); agent assembly of normal-locus argument

proof.text: Every identification above uses structural maps, germs, or the unique extension to a localization: on a fraction it sends $b/s$ to the image of $b$ times the inverse image of $s$. Hence the two composites in every restriction/localization square agree on numerators and on inverses of denominators, and therefore agree. For arbitrary open restrictions use Step 2 and test on affine neighborhoods; the component coordinates are indexed by the same generic points, with precisely the absent components omitted as in Step 6. This verifies the asserted compatibility. If $X=\varnothing$, its normalization is the empty disjoint union by [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]; the empty scheme is Noetherian, the map is finite and surjective, and $N=\varnothing$ is dense open in the empty space. There are no nonempty affine opens or points to check.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NL-615327a97 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: One fault, repaired. I read the statement, all 8 steps, every cited statement, and Stacks 035P, 0C3B and 0CDV. The statement is unchanged from the base and there are no new nodes. Mechanical finding confirmed: Step 3 cited lem-per-componentwise-normalization-affine-charts, which is on line 1474 of route-pivot-dropped.txt (section 2026-10-19 artin-gabber), and no step justifies it. Its content is generic (Stacks 035P/0CDV), so I rebuilt it from live nodes. New Step 3 uses finite minimal primes (00FR), components of Spec as V(minimal prime) (00ES), the reduced induced chart Z_i∩U=Spec R/p_i (01J3, Lean-closed), the scheme coproduct and finite affine coproduct spectrum, and finiteness of each Z_i^ν→Z_i from Step 1. Together these give ν⁻¹U=Spec ∏T_i with T_i finite and the map r↦(r mod p_i). Step 4 adds the missing hypothesis check for lem-sfb-normalization-affine-total-fractions (quasi-compact opens of a Noetherian scheme have finitely many components). It also writes out that an integral closure inside a finite product of fields is the product of the integral closures (project a monic relation; multiply lifted monics). Since any R-algebra map R̄→Q(R) is the inclusion, T=∏B_i⊆∏K_i canonically, and T_i lands on the factor B_i. I recomputed proof_deps as the union of the step uses and removed the dropped node from split_report.tool_uses, adding the reduced-induced-closed-subscheme tool. The fixed closure (170 nodes) contains no dropped id and no cycle. Steps 1, 2 and 5–8 are correct as delivered. Edge cases checked: the empty scheme, k×k, k[u,v]/(uv), and the cusp k[t²,t³]. No SGA.
